title: Classic Nashville Hot Chicken Leg Quarters
summary: Buttermilk-marinated, bone-in chicken leg quarters with an extra-crunchy seasoned flour crust, fried and tossed in a cayenne-brown sugar spice oil, served on white Texas toast with pickles.
notes: Video: 'Perfect Nashville Hot Fried Chicken At Home (2 Ways)' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). This file is one of two versions in the video (house rule 6), both pointing to the same transcript: the classic bone-in leg quarters on white toast, and a boneless tender sandwich. Written recipe for both: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/perfect-nashville-hot-fried-chicken-at-home-2-ways-recipe (serves 4, prep 30 min, cook 45 min for the page as a whole). Marinating time is not in prep_minutes (house rule 13): at least 2 hours, ideally overnight. The page gives a separate marinade for each version but one dredge and one hot-oil mix; the video says the tenders are breaded 'exactly like the leg quarters' and tossed in the spicy oil, so this file repeats the full dredge and hot oil so it stands alone. All marinade, dredge and hot-oil amounts are stated in the video and match the page. House rules applied: the buttermilk marinade is poured off and excluded; the dredge counts at 25%; the deep-frying oil is excluded and absorbed oil is counted at 10% of the raw breaded weight (arithmetic on that line). The hot spice oil (about 1 cup of the frying oil whisked into the spices) is a dunking oil made in a bigger batch than stays on the chicken and no share is stated, so every hot-oil line counts at 25% (house rule 10; full batch kept in each line's text). Optional chicken bouillon powder is counted (at 25%) because the transcript narrates it being added with the other spices (house rule 11); this is inferred from the narration, not seen on screen. The optional extra spoonful of spice oil is excluded (mentioned, not added). The cayenne in the hot oil can go up to 1/2 cup; we use 1/4 cup. Potato starch is listed as an excluded alternative to the cornstarch. Smoked paprika uses the existing paprika slug. Brown sugar is dark brown (light is allowed). Version 1 (classic): 4 servings, one leg quarter on one slice of toast each; the written recipe's 4 servings and 4 slices of Texas toast agree. From the written recipe: 4 slices Texas toast (weight ours, 40 g each). Our estimate: 12 pickle coins (72 g) for 'a few dill pickle slices'. The leg quarters are entered as bought, bone-in (2 lb, house rule 12); the lead converts to edible weight with USDA's yield for the cut. Absorbed oil uses the as-bought weight. Prep and cook times are the page's figures for both versions together.

steps.text: Whisk the buttermilk, Frank's RedHot, salt and MSG. Add the leg quarters, work the marinade under the skin and make sure they are submerged. Cover and refrigerate, ideally overnight (frying right away works but the meat is less seasoned).
Whisk the dredge: flour, cornstarch, salt, MSG, smoked paprika, cayenne and garlic powder.

In a heatproof bowl, whisk the hot-oil spices: cayenne, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, brown sugar and bouillon powder, breaking up any sugar lumps. Set aside. Wash your hands well after handling it.

With your wet hand, flick a little marinade into the dredge and toss; repeat up to three times to build small clumps. Lift each leg quarter from the marinade, press it into the flour on all sides and under the skin until there are no bare spots, then shake off the excess and set it down.
Heat oil to 325°F, ideally in two pots with two leg quarters each. Fry 12-15 minutes, to 165°F inside, watching the heat so they don't scorch on the bottom.
While they fry, ladle about 1 cup of the hot frying oil (around 350°F) into the spice mix and whisk immediately. The spices settle, so stir again before using.
As soon as the chicken comes out, toss it in the spice oil and set it on a wire rack to drain. Spoon over a little more spice oil if you want more color and heat.
Serve each leg quarter on a thick slice of white Texas toast with a few dill pickle slices.
